messages.text: My miner arrived faulty
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill

Hi, I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sorry your miner arrived with a problem. Let's work out what's wrong.

To start, could you tell me:

1. Which miner is it? For example a NerdQX, Bitaxe, Hammer DC06 or Harlo B30. If you know which order it came on, tell me that too.
2. What does it do when you plug it in? For example: no power at all, a screen error, fans not spinning, no hashrate, or damage from shipping.

If there's an error on the screen or anything is visibly damaged, a photo would help a lot.

**Safety first:** if you've noticed smoke, a burning smell, sparks or a hot plug, unplug it now and leave it unplugged.
hI sarah

Hi! This is actually Hal, the technical specialist. Sarah passed your chat to me because the miner arrived faulty, and that's the kind of problem I handle.

To get started, I just need two things:

1. **Which miner is it?** For example a NerdQX, Bitaxe, Hammer DC06 or Harlo B30.
2. **What happens when you plug it in?** For example nothing at all, an error on the screen, fans not spinning, no hashrate, or visible damage.

If you can, send a photo of the screen or of any damage.
kbox

Thanks, so it's the GekkoScience KBOX.

What happens when you plug it in? For example:

1. Nothing at all: no lights, no screen, no fan
2. It powers on but shows an error on the screen
3. It runs but isn't hashing, or the hashrate is very low
4. Something is physically damaged, like a cracked screen or a broken fan

A photo of the unit or its screen would help too.
it runs and terra hash rate go from 35 to O. the miner is in perfect condition., Lights inside the miner are too.
Searched the web · GekkoScience KBOX miner setup hashrate

Thanks, that helps. Good to hear the unit looks perfect.

The K. is rated at about 22 TH/s, so a reading of 35 followed by a drop to 0 usually points to a setting or protection issue rather than a broken board. One thing worth knowing: 
if either fan stops, hashing stops to avoid overheat
, and it also has 
software limits on ASIC temperature, hardware limits on main voltage regulator temperature
.

So my first question: **when the hashrate drops to 0, are both fans still spinning?** You should be able to see or hear them through the front grid.

If you can, please also send a screenshot of the KBOX web dashboard after it drops to 0. It should show the temperatures, fan speeds and the power preset (High, Medium or Low).
Im sorry but can you send an email to (email hidden) (phone hidden)
Handed to the team · Troubleshooting not finished: we don't yet know whether both fans keep spinning

No problem. I can't send emails from this chat, so I've passed your case to our hardware team: the KBOX, the hashrate showing about 35 TH/s then dropping to 0, and that the unit looks undamaged. They'll pick it up tomorrow at 10am ET and reply to the email on your account.

If you want an answer sooner, our Discord is very active: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf . Mention @nullhashrate (JD, our hardware lead).

When you get back to the miner, two things will speed this up:

1. Check whether both fans are still spinning when the hashrate drops to 0.
2. Take a screenshot of the KBOX dashboard after the drop.

(Handed to Sarah in support)
hash rate went to 9 when i just turned it on hit it regular 0.567 its all over the place.  The K. so far hard to recommend.

Hal here again, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist.

Thanks for checking. A hashrate that jumps around right after you turn it on doesn't mean the unit is faulty. While the miner warms up, the number is averaged over very few shares, so readings like 9 one moment and 0.567 the next are common. What counts is the number once it has settled.

Two quick things:

1. **Let it run for about 15 to 20 minutes** without touching it.
2. Then tell me **where you're reading the number**: the KBOX's own web dashboard, or a pool or EZBlockchain page? Pool pages average over longer windows and lag behind, so they can show very different numbers.

If it's still well under 22 TH/s after that, send a screenshot of the KBOX dashboard and I'll dig in from there.
Hi Sarah, can any one log into the computer / Minerminer.I have serial number

It's Hal here, Rob, the technical specialist.

Nobody can log into your miner remotely, us included. The K. dashboard is only reachable from your own home network, and a serial number doesn't give access to it. That's a good thing for your security.

You can open the dashboard yourself in a web browser. I'll walk you through it one step at a time.

**Step 1:** On a phone or computer connected to the same network as the KBOX, log into your router's app or admin page and look at the list of connected devices. Find the KBOX and tell me the IP address next to it. It usually looks like 192.168.x.x.

Hold on to the serial number. A clear photo of it will help if we need it later. Please don't share any passwords here.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Great, you're in the KBOX dashboard. That's real progress.

Your photo shows the **Device & Maintenance** section: "Check for updates", "Restart", and a red bar under Restart that says **"Network error: Failed to fetch"**.

That red message comes from your browser. It means the page lost contact with the miner for a moment. It doesn't mean the miner is broken. The most likely causes:

- you just clicked Restart or Check for updates, so the miner went offline briefly, or
- the miner rebooted or dropped off the network by itself. That would also explain the hashrate falling to 0 and climbing back up.

**Next step:**

1. Did you click Restart (or Check for updates) just before that red bar appeared?
2. Wait about a minute, refresh the page (press F5), and scroll to the **top** of the dashboard. Send me a photo of that part. It shows the hashrate, temperatures, fan speeds and firmware version, which is what I need to pin this down.

Please don't press **Factory Reset** for now. We may not need it.
I have lots it only lets me send one at a time?

Yes, the chat only takes one picture at a time. Send them one after another and I'll look at each one as it arrives.

To save you time, these are the ones I need most, in this order:

1. **The top of the dashboard**: hashrate, temperatures and fan speeds.
2. **The firmware or software version**, if it's shown somewhere.
3. **Anything with a red or yellow warning** on it.

Start with the first one whenever you're ready.
O Damn, sorry to have missed you.

You didn't miss me, Rob. I'm still here.

Whenever you're ready, send the first photo: **the top of the KBOX dashboard**, with the hashrate, temperatures and fan speeds. Then send the others one at a time.
ok wont touch

Perfect, thanks Rob. Leave Factory Reset alone for now.

Next, scroll to the very top of the dashboard page and send me a photo of it. I'm after the hashrate, temperatures and fan speeds.
you want one at a time I have a few more but i think you understand

I appreciate it, Rob, but so far I've only received one photo: the Device & Maintenance section with the "Failed to fetch" bar. That one alone doesn't tell me why the hashrate drops.

The photo that will crack this is **the top of the dashboard** (hashrate, temperatures, fan speeds). Please send that one next, and the others after it if you like. I'll check each one as it comes in.
